variants.headline: Looking back: money in hand, no food to buy
variants.sub: People have money for food but cannot buy it because shops and farms are sold out.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: Shops and farms were sold out of food, leaving people with money unable to buy meals.

Effective demand cannot produce an immediate sale from an exhausted supply. Commercial readers should identify this as an availability problem, rather than automatically infer inadequate household funds. A useful assessment distinguishes the buyer's means from the goods on offer and asks what practical provision requires on the supply side.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We defend {target} against indiscriminate blame. The lack of available food is serious, but it does not establish every claim about its cause or prove that an imagined alternative would supply the missing meals.
